categories.main_business_segments: Electronic Arts (EA) operates as a single reportable segment focused on developing, marketing, publishing, and delivering digital interactive entertainment. Its primary business lines include the creation and distribution of games, content, and services for consoles, PCs, and mobile devices, with a portfolio of wholly owned and licensed franchises such as Apex Legends, Battlefield, The Sims, Madden NFL, and the global football (soccer) franchise.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: EA leverages proprietary and licensed technologies to develop high-quality, innovative games and live services. The company invests in advanced software development, including self-learning artificial intelligence, robust online infrastructure for live services, and cross-platform compatibility. Game development is managed by internal studios and external partners, with a focus on continuous updates, live operations, and digital content delivery.
categories.primary_customers_markets: EA primarily serves individual consumers who play video games on consoles, PCs, and mobile devices. Its key markets include gamers interested in sports, action, simulation, and role-playing genres, with a significant focus on sports fans through annualized franchises like FIFA (transitioning to EA SPORTS FC) and Madden NFL. The company also targets online communities and players seeking ongoing engagement through live services and extra content.
categories.geographic_coverage: EA operates globally, with significant revenue generated in North America and internationally. In fiscal 2023, 58% of net revenue was from international markets, with Switzerland serving as a major hub for international business. The company has partnerships and distribution agreements in Asia (notably China and Korea), and its games are available worldwide through digital and retail channels.
categories.supply_chain_position: EA operates downstream in the supply chain as a publisher and distributor of finished digital entertainment products and services. It manages the end-user experience, including game development, marketing, sales, and ongoing live service operations, while relying on platform partners (e.g., Sony, Microsoft, Apple, Google) for distribution and access to hardware ecosystems.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: EA's strategic priorities center on expanding live services, growing global online communities around key franchises, and increasing re-occurring revenue streams. The company invests heavily in R&D to drive innovation in gameplay, artificial intelligence, and interactive storytelling, while also exploring new business models such as free-to-play and subscriptions. Portfolio rationalization and targeted acquisitions support its focus on high-growth opportunities.
categories.revenue_model: EA generates revenue through a mix of digital and physical full game sales, live services (including extra content, in-game purchases, and downloadable content), subscriptions (e.g., EA Play), and licensing arrangements. Live services, particularly extra content for Ultimate Team modes and Apex Legends, account for the majority of revenue, with digital channels representing a growing share of total sales.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: EA faces intense competition from established interactive entertainment companies (e.g., Activision Blizzard, Take-Two Interactive, Ubisoft), large technology firms expanding into gaming (e.g., Microsoft, Sony, Apple, Google), and new market entrants. The company is a global leader in sports and simulation genres, with top market positions in football (soccer) and American football games, but must continuously innovate to maintain its competitive edge.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ended March 31, 2023, EA reported net revenue of $7.4 billion, up 6% year-over-year, with live services accounting for 74% of total revenue. Operating income was $1.3 billion, and net income was $802 million. The company maintains a strong balance sheet with $2.8 billion in cash and short-term investments, and continues to invest in growth through R&D, acquisitions, and shareholder returns.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: EA differentiates itself through a portfolio of leading intellectual properties, high-quality and innovative game experiences, and robust live services that drive ongoing player engagement. The company emphasizes its ability to deliver entertainment across multiple platforms and business models, leveraging strong brand recognition, global reach, and a network of hundreds of millions of active accounts to create value for players and partners.
